Guidance & outlook: Standalone revenue from our operation increased by 71.1% year-on-year to INR 505 crores, compared to INR 295 crores in Q1 of FY2026.
Our order book as on June 2026, including order received post June, was INR 541 crores, providing visibility for execution over coming quarter.
I just wanted to highlight, the management recently said that they are targeting approximately INR 3,000 crores in revenue.
Growth & demand: The current unexecuted order book of around INR 541 crores seems relatively modest compared to the company's growth aspirations.
See, if you see the growth trajectory in last couple of years, you will see that quarter one always remains 15% to 20% of our annual volume.
But when I'm comparing my order book, so I have a 20% order book from the rooftop and 80% from the pump.
Margins & costs: EBITDA increased by 47.7% to INR 86.1 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 17.05%.

We control critical raw material and work with multiple manufacturing partners, allowing us to maintain quality, supply availability, and cost efficiency while keeping fixed capital requirement relatively low.
Yes, realization has been low per pump, but the overall volume is growing up.
Capex & expansion: With commissioning of 109 MW of renewable energy capacity during the quarter, with this, our cumulative installation base has crossed 1,64,500 systems and 726 MW of renewable energy capacity in decentralized way.
Our growth strategy continue to build around technology defined low capex model supported by our OEM/ODM manufacturing ecosystem.
Our decentralized warehousing, logistics, and field execution network further enable us to scale across geography without requiring proportionate investment in fixed infrastructure.
Balance sheet & cash: So, first of all, we were having the surplus cash available with the company because we have very good receivable done in the financial year ending in the March.
And we are right now raised the fund through the IPO for the working capital.
So, that is also supporting us for not having the bank debt.
Risks & challenges: Because a lot of news flow for every company depends on that, and we are seeing lackluster performance by few of the companies in the sector because of the delays, basically.
And it has to get started because if it gets delayed, then overall scheme will get impact.

At the same time, we ended FY26 with the net surplus cash and cash equivalent is INR 240 crores compared to net debt position of INR 155 crores in FY25, which it's a very good positive acceleration growth symptom for us to go ahead.

Sir, my question was the INR 3,000 crores expected revenue which we have for FY27, out of that we are expecting 1,400 orders in H1 in which I think we can execute INR 1,000 crores to INR 1,200 crores of revenue in H1.
Growth & demand: If I talk about the EBITDA level, then in standalone EBITDA for the year is INR 313 crores with 53.49% growth comparatively to INR 204 crores in last year.
It is a 51% Y-o-Y growth comparatively to INR 133 crores last year.
So, revenue side from the solar system installation of decentralized system, it came to INR 418.57 crores with Y-o-Y last year it was INR 352 crores with the good growth.
Margins & costs: This is having the margin expanding to 20.44% compared to 18.64% in FY25.
In consolidated level, we have done the business of INR 1,715 crores with EBITDA of INR 318 crores with the PAT of INR 204.3 crores.

So, we have done the INR 199 crores business including into our wholly-owned subsidiary for the DCR cells securing, because we secured our raw material, and for that, we have this our subsidiary to do this work.
Capex & expansion: We have reached to the 15,000 plus monthly installation capacity right now.
And we occupy their 30%, 40% to 50% of manufacturing capacity.
So, I have to not made any INR 300 crores, INR 400 crores, INR 500 crores investment in capex mode.

And if I even if if around 30% is the working capital intensity, which means we need INR 1,000 crores of working capital requirement.

So, worst case we are talking about INR 2,500 crores revenue and the best case can be INR 3,000 crores revenue if the PM-KUSUM 2.0 is not delayed.

Guidance & outlook: EBITDA for H1 from business was INR 132.04 crores; it is basically 65.07% increase over INR 79.99 crores last year, with EBITDA margin expanding to 20.20% compared to 18.96% in H1 FY 2025.

At the same time, profit after tax came in at INR 83.40 crores, marking a 63.26% YoY growth increase positive side over INR 51.08 crores in the previous year PAT margin, also improved from 12.76% compared to 12.11% in H1 FY 2025.
It is a 50.77% increase over the 16,251 pumps in the last year FY 2025 H1.
Growth & demand: It represented 51.75% YoY growth compared to INR 419.66 crores in H1 Financial Year 2025.
Coming to the 2nd Quarter more specifically: Revenue from core EPC business of solar pump and rooftop was INR 358.50 crores, delivering a 33.06% YoY growth over INR 269.42 crores in Q2 of FY2025.
PAT for the quarter was INR 46.46 crores, showing a growth of 36.01% YoY increase over the INR 34.16 crores in Quarter 2 FY 2025.
Margins & costs: EBITDA for the quarter came in around INR 73.74 crores, up by 37.63% from INR 53.58 crores last year, with EBITDA margin at INR 20.57 crores versus INR 19.83 crores for the similar quarter last year for the comparison.
For the H1 FY 2026, our consolidated revenue from operations stood 728.83 crores with EBITDA at 132.74 crores and PAT at 84.23 crores.
And our EBITDA margin will remain same, or it is going to improve more positively.
Capex & expansion: Further, we would also had a small order book of around 17.83 crores related to the rooftop solar project, that is representing around further 4 megawatt of the capacity, or we can say 4,000 kilowatt of the capacity to be installed.
We are targeting to increase around 25% to 30% capacity without stretch in comfort zone.
So, current capacity is up to 10,000 per month that we are going to increase 25, 30% like that.
Balance sheet & cash: We have looked towards a little bit delay into the receivable from the previous time; it was 135 to 192 days in September 2024 to September 2025.
These are the three, four reasons accounting for the overall delay into the receivable cycle, but all are expected to be normalized in due course of the time.
We are 100% and fully confident for the third quarter that we will have the receivable very well under control.
Risks & challenges: That has been got delayed because the monsoon was very aggressive this year in the whole area where we are working.

We have been into the software integration as we are growing, so there was software integration to be took place, and some software upgradation while sending the RMS data has took some delay, as well as we were occupied on the IPO work and other activities.
So, I do not get that pressure of the margin going down, that pressure gets transferred in the whole ecosystem.
